SELECTED_INDEX: 7
CONFIDENCE: 0.30
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows features typical for an organophosphorothioate.  
• A strong P=S stretch appears in Raman near 600–700 cm⁻¹; the band at 566 cm⁻¹ fits this (rule‐of‐thumb for P=S).  
• O-,S-substituted phosphorus compounds give P–O–C stretches in the 900–1030 cm⁻¹ region; the intense doublet at 935 / 919 cm⁻¹ and the 847 cm⁻¹ band correspond well.  
• Phosphorus compounds that contain a P=O or P=S bond often show a band near 1250 cm⁻¹; the 1259 cm⁻¹ peak matches this thio-phosphoryl deformation.  
• Alkyl C–H stretches at 2880–2950 cm⁻¹ and CH₂/CH₃ bending at 1454 cm⁻¹ confirm an aliphatic molecule.  

Among the candidates, only “CCP(O)(O)=S” (index 7) contains the required P=S bond together with P–O and P–C linkages that can account for the 566, 935/919 and 847 cm⁻¹ bands, while also matching the aliphatic C–H features. Other candidates either lack phosphorus, lack sulfur, or would introduce characteristic high-frequency modes (e.g., N=C=S, C≡C, N=C=O) that are absent from the experimental spectrum.
